tasks.title: CLP/JPY/KWD amounts rendered with the wrong number of decimals
tasks.summary: Fixed PAY-4411: `money.Amount.Decimal()` hardcoded division by 100 and `%02d`, so zero-decimal currencies (CLP, JPY) and three-decimal currencies (KWD) rendered wrong. Rewrote it to use the currency's `Exponent` and `Factor()`: exponent 0 renders as a plain integer (e.g. 15000 CLP), exponent 2 renders with 2 decimals (USD unchanged), exponent 3 renders with 3 decimals (e.g. 1.234 KWD). Negative amounts keep the minus sign. All existing tests, `go vet`, and gofmt pass.

tasks.title: Multiple partial refunds can exceed the captured amount
tasks.summary:
Fixed PAY-4420: total refunds could exceed the payment amount.

Root cause: in payment/service.go, the Refund method validated the requested amount against the full payment amount (`p.Amount.Minor`) instead of the remaining amount, so each refund was allowed up to the full payment value regardless of prior refunds.

Fix: changed the guard to compare against `p.Amount.Minor - p.Refunded` (the remaining amount). A refund larger than what is left is now rejected with ErrRefundExceedsRemaining (mapped to 422 refund_exceeds_remaining in api/errors.go) and does not mutate the payment. Refunding exactly the remaining amount is still allowed and moves the payment to REFUNDED.

Added TestRefundExceedsRemainingAfterPartial covering the reported scenario (600 + 600 on a 1000 payment) plus the exact-remaining refund path.

tasks.title: Cursor pagination silently drops one payment per page
tasks.summary:
Fixed PAY-4432: reconciliation missing payments when paging.

Root cause: in store/memory.go ListByMerchant, the cursor encodes `end` — the index immediately after the last item returned on the previous page. The next page should resume at exactly that offset, but the code incremented the decoded offset (`offset++`), skipping one item on every page after the first. With 1000 payments and limit=50 that skipped 19 items (981 collected); with limit=1 it skipped every other item (~half).

Fix: removed the erroneous `offset++` so paging resumes at the cursor position. The last-page logic (`end < len(ids)` → empty next_cursor) already handles exact multiples correctly.

Added TestListWalksAllPages which seeds 1000 payments for merchant m_204 and walks all pages for limits 1, 2, 7, 50, 100, 500, asserting every payment is returned exactly once in creation order and next_cursor is empty on the last page.

tasks.title: Webhook dispatcher retries permanent 4xx failures and gives up on 5xx
tasks.summary:
Fixed PAY-4450: the webhook `retryable` predicate in `webhook/dispatcher.go` had its retry classification backwards.

The old logic retried all 4xx responses (`status >= 400 && status < 500`) but not 5xx, which caused:
- m_77: permanent client errors (400/401/404/410) were retried MaxAttempts times instead of going straight to the dead-letter list.
- m_91: transient server errors (503) were treated as permanent and dead-lettered after a single attempt.

Changed `retryable` to match the README policy: transport errors, 408, 429, and 5xx (`status >= 500`) are retried with backoff up to MaxAttempts; any other non-2xx status is permanent and goes straight to the dead-letter list.

Dead-letter recording was already correct: `deliver` records the number of attempts and the last HTTP status (e.g. Attempts=1/LastStatus=410 for a permanent 4xx, Attempts=MaxAttempts/LastStatus=503 for exhausted 5xx retries). Verified with `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `gofmt -l .` — all clean.

tasks.title: Idempotency keys never expire after 24h
tasks.summary:
Fixed PAY-4461 (Idempotency-Key replays after the 24h TTL) in `idempotency/store.go`:

1. `Begin` now only applies replay/reuse/in-progress semantics when the stored record is still live (`now.Before(r.ExpiresAt)`). Once a key is expired (`now >= ExpiresAt`), the expired record is evicted and a brand-new request begins regardless of fingerprint — behaving as if the key had never been used. This fixes the merchant reusing a key 40h later and getting the old cached response.

2. `purgeLocked` was evicting records only when `now.Sub(r.ExpiresAt) > m.ttl` (i.e. 24h *after* expiry = ~48h total), which is why memory grew for two days. Changed the condition to `!now.Before(r.ExpiresAt)` so expired records are evicted at expiry on the next purge cycle (throttled to DefaultPurgeInterval).

Before-expiry semantics (replay, ErrKeyReuse, ErrInProgress) are unchanged. Public APIs and constructors are unchanged.

Added tests `TestExpiredKeyStartsNewRequest` (expired key starts a fresh request even with a different fingerprint, and the new response is the one replayed afterward) and `TestExpiredRecordEvicted` (expired record is purged from memory). All existing tests, `go vet`, and gofmt remain clean.

tasks.title: Every client error is returned as 500 internal_error
tasks.summary: Fixed PAY-4475: api/errorResponse now matches domain errors with errors.Is instead of direct equality (switch err). Since the service wraps all errors with fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err), the previous direct comparison failed and every domain error (not-found, invalid transition/conflict, over-refund, invalid input) fell through to 500 internal_error. Now wrapped errors are correctly mapped to their documented status codes and error codes (404 not_found, 409 invalid_transition/conflict, 422 refund_exceeds_remaining, 400 invalid_request), while unexpected errors remain 500 with a generic message. Build, go vet, gofmt, and go test -race ./... all pass.

tasks.title: Late webhook retries fire with no delay
tasks.summary:
Fixed PAY-4488: the webhook retry storm.

Root cause: `Policy.Backoff` computed the wait as `p.BaseDelay << (n - 1)`. For enterprise policies (BaseDelay 1s, MaxDelay 1h, MaxAttempts 48) the left shift overflows time.Duration's int64 around attempt 35, producing a negative value. The cap check `d > p.MaxDelay` then fails (negative < positive MaxDelay), so a negative duration was returned and `clock.Sleep` returned immediately — firing the remaining retries back-to-back.

Fix in webhook/dispatcher.go: rewrote Backoff to double step-by-step with an overflow guard, capping at MaxDelay as soon as the running value reaches/exceeds it. The result is always positive, non-decreasing in n, and capped at MaxDelay for any attempt number and reasonable BaseDelay/MaxDelay. Degenerate inputs (non-positive BaseDelay/MaxDelay) are handled defensively.

Added TestBackoffEnterpriseNoStorm regression test covering the enterprise policy across all 48 attempts. Existing tests and `go vet`/gofmt remain clean.

tasks.title: Add payment cancellation (CANCELED status + endpoint + webhook)
tasks.summary:
Implemented PAY-4502 (cancel a payment before capture):

- payment/payment.go: added StatusCanceled ("CANCELED"), registered it in allStatuses (so ParseStatus accepts it case-insensitively), and made Status.Final() return true for it.
- payment/service.go: added Service.Cancel(ctx, id), allowed only from CREATED/PENDING (else ErrInvalidTransition), reusing the existing mutate helper so unknown ids wrap ErrNotFound. It emits the "payment.canceled" event, delivered as a webhook like the other events. Because CANCELED is not in the allowed cases of Authorize/Capture/Decline/Refund, a canceled payment can no longer be authorized, captured, declined or refunded (409).
- api/handlers.go + api/server.go: added POST /payments/{id}/cancel handler and route, returning 200 with the payment body (status "CANCELED"), 409 invalid_transition when not cancelable, and 404 not_found for unknown ids (via the existing errorResponse mapping).

All existing tests pass with go test -race, go vet, and gofmt are clean.

tasks.title: Filter the merchant payment listing by status
tasks.summary:
Implemented status filtering for the merchant payments listing endpoint (PAY-4510).

Changes:
- payment/payment.go: added an optional `Status` field to `Page` (empty = no filter), keeping the public API backward compatible.
- store/memory.go: `ListByMerchant` now filters the merchant's payment IDs by `page.Status` before applying the offset/limit window, so the existing offset-based cursor paginates over the filtered set in creation order. Every page except the last is full, walking next_cursor returns each match exactly once, and next_cursor is empty after the last match.
- api/handlers.go: `listPayments` parses the optional `status` query parameter via `payment.ParseStatus` (case-insensitive). An unknown status yields `ErrInvalidInput`, which maps to 400 invalid_request. Without `status` the request behaves exactly as before.

Tests added:
- store/memory_test.go: `TestListByStatus` and `TestListByStatusPaginates` covering filtering, ordering, empty results, and full-page pagination over interleaved non-matching payments.
- api/api_test.go: `TestListPaymentsByStatus` (case-insensitive filter + 400 on unknown status) and `TestListPaymentsByStatusPaginates` (end-to-end pagination walking each match once with no duplicates).

All existing tests, `go vet`, and `gofmt` remain clean.

tasks.title: Replay a dead-lettered webhook event
tasks.summary:
Implemented PAY-4523: ops can re-deliver dead-lettered webhooks.

webhook package (dispatcher.go):
- Added exported error `ErrDeadLetterNotFound`.
- Added `func (d *Dispatcher) Replay(ctx context.Context, eventID string) (delivered bool, err error)`. It removes the matching event from the dead-letter list and re-runs the normal `deliver` path (same id/payload, signature recomputed at send time, normal retry policy). On success returns (true, nil) with the event no longer dead-lettered; on a fresh failure returns (false, nil) with the event back in the dead-letter list exactly once reflecting the new attempts/status; unknown id returns an error wrapping `ErrDeadLetterNotFound`. If ctx is cancelled mid-delivery the event is re-dead-lettered and the error is returned.
- Added `SetSender` helper to swap the sender (used by tests).

api package:
- New route `POST /webhooks/dead-letters/{eventID}/replay` handled by `replayDeadLetter`, returning `200 {"event_id": "...", "delivered": true|false}`; unknown id maps to 404 not_found via `errorResponse` (added `webhook.ErrDeadLetterNotFound` mapping).
- Added `replayResponse` DTO.

Tests added in webhook_test.go (Replay success, replay fails again, unknown id) and api_test.go (replay endpoint 200/404). All existing tests, go vet, gofmt, and `go test -race ./...` pass.

tasks.title: Accept and return integer minor units, backward compatible
tasks.summary:
Implemented PAY-4530: API v2 integer minor-unit amounts, backward compatible.

Changes in api/dto.go:
- createPaymentRequest and refundRequest gained an optional `amount_minor *int64` JSON field alongside the legacy `amount` string.
- paymentResponse adds integer fields `amount_minor`, `fee_minor`, `refunded_minor`, `remaining_minor`; each refundResponse adds `amount_minor`. All existing fields are unchanged.
- toPaymentResponse populates the new fields from the payment aggregate.

Changes in api/handlers.go:
- Added resolveAmount(amount string, amountMinor *int64, code string) which enforces the rules: exactly one of amount/amount_minor is required (neither -> 400 invalid_request); if only the string is present it is parsed; if only the integer is present it is built via money.New; if both are present they must denote the same minor value (mismatch -> 400 invalid_request).
- createPayment and refundPayment now use resolveAmount (refund uses the payment's currency).

Idempotency: createFingerprint/refundFingerprint already hash the resolved Amount.Minor and currency code, so a retry using the other format for the same value produces the same fingerprint and is replayed (covered by a new cross-format test).

Unknown JSON fields remain rejected because decodeJSON keeps DisallowUnknownFields; amount_minor is now a known field.

Added tests covering: amount_minor create, both-formats-agree, neither/both-disagree/bad-currency/unknown-field validation, refund via amount_minor, refund disagreement, cross-format idempotent replay, and the new response fields. go build, go vet, gofmt, and go test -race ./... all pass.

tasks.title: Centralize the payment status machine in one transition table
tasks.summary: Added `CanTransition(from, to Status) bool` in payment/payment.go as the single source of truth for allowed status transitions (CREATED->PENDING, CREATED->DECLINED, PENDING->SUCCEEDED, PENDING->DECLINED, SUCCEEDED->REFUNDED; no self transitions). Refactored Authorize, Capture, Decline, and Refund in payment/service.go to validate transitions through CanTransition, removing all `switch p.Status` statements. Refund uses CanTransition(p.Status, StatusRefunded) to gate both partial and full refunds (a partial refund is allowed exactly when a full refund would be). Public behaviour, events, returned payments and wrapped errors are unchanged. Build, vet, gofmt, and the full test suite (with -race) pass.

tasks.title: Idempotency store is not safe under concurrent retries
tasks.summary:
Fixed PAY-4555: idempotency.Memory is now safe for concurrent use and guarantees at most one concurrent Begin starts a request per key.

Root cause: Begin released the lock between the lookup and the insert, so two concurrent retries with the same key could both observe "no record" and both start (duplicate refunds). Complete and Release also read/wrote the map without holding the lock (concurrent map read/write crash).

Changes in idempotency/store.go:
- Begin now performs the purge, lookup, and reservation atomically under a single held lock (deferred unlock). For a given key only the first caller gets started=true; concurrent callers get ErrInProgress (or the stored response once completed).
- Complete now locks the mutex before reading/writing the record.
- Release now locks the mutex before the existence check and delete (no more unlocked map read).
- purgeLocked contract documented as requiring the caller to hold m.mu.

Added concurrency regression tests in idempotency/store_test.go (TestBeginConcurrentSingleStarter, TestConcurrentCompleteReleaseRace). go test -race, go vet, and gofmt all pass.

tasks.title: In-memory repository shares mutable state with callers
tasks.summary:
PAY-4561: Fixed the data race and phantom-refund bug in store.Memory.

Root cause: Payment is a value type but contains a `Refunds []Refund` slice. `Memory.Get` returned the map value by struct copy, so the returned `Refunds` slice header shared its backing array with the stored payment. `Memory.Update`/`Create`/`ListByMerchant` likewise stored shallow copies. Under concurrent `Refund` calls on the same payment, each goroutine loaded the payment via Get, appended a refund to its local copy, and raced on the shared backing array. Worse, when a refund's `Update` lost the optimistic-lock race (version conflict), the `append` had already written the new refund id into the shared backing array of the stored payment's `Refunds` slice — leaving a phantom refund whose amount was never added to `Refunded`, so `refunds` no longer summed to `refunded_amount`.

Fix: `store.Memory` now deep-copies payments on the way in and out via `Payment.Clone()`:
- `Get` returns `p.Clone()`
- `Create` stores `p.Clone()`
- `Update` stores `next := p.Clone()` (version bump on the clone)
- `ListByMerchant` appends `m.byID[id].Clone()`

This guarantees values handed to or returned by the repository never share mutable state with what is stored, so a failed update leaves no trace and concurrent operations are race-free. Optimistic-locking semantics (version compare + increment, ErrVersionConflict) are unchanged. The in-test `fakeRepo` already cloned, matching this contract.

Added regression tests in store/memory_race_test.go: TestConcurrentRefundsNoRaceNoPhantom fires 50 concurrent refunds and asserts no unexpected errors, stored Refunds sum == Refunded, refund count == successful ops, and no duplicate/empty ids; TestGetReturnsIndependentCopy asserts mutating a Get result cannot corrupt stored state.

tasks.title: Idempotency Begin gets slower with every stored key
tasks.summary:
PAY-4570: Fixed POST latency growing with traffic in idempotency.(*Memory).Begin.

Root cause: Begin called purgeLocked on every request, and purgeLocked was O(n log n) — it copied every record into a slice and sorted it by ExpiresAt. With tens of thousands of live keys, each POST paid that cost, so p99 grew with store size and only recovered on pod restart (which cleared the map).

Changes in idempotency/store.go:
- Rate-limited eviction: Begin only runs the purge when at least `purgeInterval` (1 minute) has elapsed since the last purge, tracked via a new `lastPurge` field. Between purges Begin is O(1) (a single map lookup), so its cost no longer depends on the number of stored keys.
- Made purgeLocked a single O(n) pass that deletes every record with `now >= ExpiresAt`, dropping the expensive sort/copy.
- Preserved expiry semantics: the Begin lookup still checks `now.Before(r.ExpiresAt)`, so expired keys are never replayed and can be reused (including with a new fingerprint) even before the next purge runs. Expired records are still evicted on the periodic purge, keeping memory bounded (at most once per minute).

Added regression tests in idempotency/store_test.go: expired keys are not replayed between purges, expired keys accept a new fingerprint, expired records are evicted (and live ones survive) once the purge interval elapses, and Begin stays cheap with 50k live keys. Existing tests, go vet, gofmt, and `go test -race ./...` all pass.

tasks.title: Split payouts do not reconcile with the charged amount
tasks.summary:
PAY-4588: Fixed money.Allocate so marketplace split payouts always reconcile.

Root cause: Allocate used float64 (violating the package's "floating point is never used for money" rule) and rounded each part independently, so the parts could sum to less or more than the original amount (e.g. 100.00/3 -> 33.33x3=99.99; 0.05/2 -> 0.03+0.03=0.06).

Fix: rewrote Allocate with exact integer arithmetic using the largest-remainder method (math/big to avoid overflow). Each part gets floor(a.Minor*r/total); the leftover minor units (a.Minor - sum of floors) are distributed one each to the parts with the largest fractional remainder, ties broken by lower index. This guarantees the parts sum exactly to a, each part is within one minor unit of its exact share, and leftover goes to the largest remainders — matching the documented contract.

Added tests (TestAllocateReconciles, TestAllocateLargestRemainder) covering the ticket's scenarios (100.00/3, 0.10/7, 0.05/2) plus the existing 1:1:2 case. All money tests, go build, go vet, gofmt, and go test -race ./... pass.

tasks.title: Identical retries rejected as idempotency key reuse
tasks.summary:
PAY-4593: Retries with the same Idempotency-Key were rejected as idempotency_key_reused because the idempotency fingerprint was computed from the raw request body bytes. When the mobile SDK rebuilds the JSON on retry (reordered keys, lowercased currency "usd" vs "USD", reformatted amount "10.5" vs "10.50"), the fingerprint changed and the store treated the retry as a different request.

Fix: compute the idempotency fingerprint from the *semantic* request instead of the raw bytes.
- createPayment now fingerprints `path | merchant_id | amount.Minor | currency.Code` (currency normalized via money.Parse/LookupCurrency, amount normalized to minor units).
- refundPayment now fingerprints `path | amount.Minor` (amount parsed in the payment's currency, so "5.00" and "5" match).
- Removed the now-unused bodyFingerprint helper (which hashed raw bytes) and its imports from api/idempotency.go; kept hash().

This makes equivalent retries replay the original stored response, while genuinely different requests (different merchant/amount/currency) still produce a different fingerprint and are rejected as idempotency_key_reused. Added tests TestIdempotentCreateReplaysEquivalentRetries and TestIdempotentRefundReplaysEquivalentRetries covering the exact SDK scenarios from the ticket. All existing tests, go vet, and gofmt pass.

tasks.title: Processing fees overcharged by one cent
tasks.summary:
Fixed PAY-4601: merchants were overcharged because money.Fee used math.Ceil (round up) instead of the documented finance policy of round-half-to-even (banker's rounding), and used float64 which loses precision on very large minor-unit amounts.

Rewrote money/fee.go to compute the fee with exact integer arithmetic using math/big:
- fee = a.Minor * bps / 10000, rounded half-to-even.
- Compares 2*remainder against the denominator to decide down/up, and on exact ties rounds to the even quotient.
- Guards the result with IsInt64 to stay within the Amount type's range.

This makes 10.05 USD at 290 bps return 0.29 (29 minor) instead of 0.30, and keeps large-ticket volumes exact. Added tests covering the bug scenario, banker's rounding tie-breaking, and a large-amount case.
